title: Face unlock
subtitle: how your phone knows you
facts: Some phones, such as iPhones with Face ID, unlock with a 3D depth scan rather than a flat photo. Other phones' face unlock only uses the normal camera, hence "some phones".
Apple: the dot projector projects more than 30,000 invisible infrared dots onto your face.
Apple: an infrared camera reads the dot pattern to build a depth map of your face.
Apple: the face data is encrypted and stays on the device, protected by the Secure Enclave; it is compared with the stored data to unlock.
Apple states the chance a random person could unlock it is about 1 in 1,000,000 (with one appearance enrolled). The script attributes this figure to Apple.

scenes.text: Some [phones] unlock by [measuring] your face in [3D].
An infrared [camera] reads how they [land], building a [depth] map.
It [compares] it to a map [stored] safely on the [phone], then [unlocks].
By [Apple's] count, a random [stranger] has [about] a [one-in-a-million] chance.
